ROLE: Finish and forget sessions: close a CLOSING session whose queued output is fully drained, then destroy and remove every CLOSED session, re-checking the new element at each index because removal shifts the tail down.

STRUCT.NAME: struct broker
STRUCT.ROLE: registry whose session array is compacted in place

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: each registry entry inspected for CLOSING/CLOSED state

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: queued-output buffer whose len decides whether a CLOSING session may be closed now

FUNC.NAME: session_state
FUNC.ROLE: read the lifecycle state of the current entry

FUNC.NAME: session_output
FUNC.ROLE: borrow the queue to test whether all queued output was flushed

FUNC.NAME: session_close_immediately
FUNC.ROLE: close a drained CLOSING session once

FUNC.NAME: remove_session_at
FUNC.ROLE: destroy the session and shift the tail down

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSING
VAR.ROLE: state that means no more output will ever be queued for this session

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSED
VAR.ROLE: state whose entry is destroyed and removed from the registry

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_state
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the current lifecycle state of the session: SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT, SESSION_READY, SESSION_CLOSING or SESSION_CLOSED; SESSION_CLOSED for a NULL session
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: read-only; nothing is modified or retained
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; the caller must treat any state other than CLOSING/CLOSED as keep

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_output
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: borrowed pointer to the queued-output buffer of the session (NULL only for a NULL session); len is the number of bytes still owed to the peer and is 0 exactly when the queue is drained or was never used
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed; the session keeps the storage, the callee only reads len here
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a NULL result means 'cannot prove drained', so the session is kept

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_close_immediately
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the session's queued output is released, its descriptor is closed once and its state becomes SESSION_CLOSED (no-op when already CLOSED)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases session-owned descriptor and queue storage; the session object itself survives until remove_session_at
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; repeated calls are no-ops

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: remove_session_at
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: static void remove_session_at(struct broker *b, size_t index)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the session at index is destroyed (descriptor closed once, buffers, identifier and filter copies freed) and the entries after it are shifted down by one so that b->count decreases by exactly one
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: consumes the session pointer held by the slot; after the call the slot holds what the previous slot i+1 held, so the element now at index must be inspected before index is advanced
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a NULL slot or out-of-range index is ignored

LOGIC.INPUT: b: the broker registry to compact; NULL is tolerated. No other parameters. The registry array element b->sessions[i] may be NULL (it never is in normal operation, but removal must not read through a NULL entry).
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If b == NULL, return. 2. i = 0. 3. While i < b->count: s = b->sessions[i]; if s == NULL, i++ and continue. 4. state = session_state(s). 5. If state == SESSION_CLOSING: out = session_output(s); if out != NULL and out->len == 0, call session_close_immediately(s) (releases the descriptor, frees the drained queue, sets SESSION_CLOSED), then set state = SESSION_CLOSED and fall through; otherwise leave the session CLOSING with its bytes intact and go to step 8. 6. If state == SESSION_CLOSED: call remove_session_at(b, i) which destroys the session and shifts the tail down, and do NOT increment i, because the element that was at i+1 is now at i and must be inspected by the next iteration (this makes adjacent victims collapse in one pass). 7. Otherwise (AWAITING_CONNECT or READY): i++ to keep the session. 8. Loop back to step 3. 9. Return; the registry contains only live sessions and CLOSING sessions that still owe bytes.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: void. Post-state: every session that was CLOSED is destroyed and removed, every drained CLOSING session has been closed and removed in the same pass, every CLOSING session with queued bytes is kept in CLOSING with its queue unchanged, and AWAITING_CONNECT/READY sessions are untouched. b->count decreases by exactly the number of removed entries; brokers that own no sessions are unchanged. A NULL broker is an accepted no-op.
INVARIANTS_USED: a CLOSING session has discarded its receive buffer and will never queue new output, so an empty queue means nothing more can be owed to the peer
clearing a length does not release storage: closing a drained CLOSING session is what releases its queue storage
removal shifts the tail down, so the index must not be advanced after a removal
the registry is owned entirely by the broker; a caller only borrows session pointers, which reaping invalidates
closing one session never affects the state of any other session
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: b is a live registry created by broker_create, or NULL. Every pointer in b->sessions[0 .. b->count-1] is either NULL or a session owned by this broker.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: no CLOSED session remains in the registry; every removed session's descriptor, buffers, identifier copy and filter copies have been released exactly once; CLOSING sessions with queued output remain until their bytes are flushed and broker_reap runs again.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded reactor; called between epoll_wait batches and from the teardown path, never concurrently.
